topicsShown.title: Say hello and tell your name
topicsShown.goal: Greet a new friend, say your name, and take a turn to talk.
topicsShown.why: You will meet new friends, so this helps you start talking with them.

topicsShown.title: Ask where a book is
topicsShown.goal: Ask where something is in the library and find it.
topicsShown.why: You can ask for help in a new place, like a library or shop.

topicsShown.title: Talk about your favourite animal
topicsShown.goal: Say what your favourite animal is and give one or two simple reasons.
topicsShown.why: Telling people what you like helps them get to know you.

topicsShown.title: Tell what you did at the weekend
topicsShown.goal: Tell three short things you did, in order, using first, then and last.
topicsShown.why: Telling what you did helps friends know your day and share their own.

topicsShown.title: Suggest a game to play
topicsShown.goal: Suggest a game, hear a reply, and agree on one game to play together.
topicsShown.why: Making plans with friends at break time is a common thing to do.

topicsShown.title: Ask someone to say it again
topicsShown.goal: Tell someone you did not understand and ask them to repeat it.
topicsShown.why: Asking again is how you can understand new words and people.

topicsShown.title: Talk about the creeper
topicsShown.goal: Describe a creeper and say if you like it or not, using short sentences.
topicsShown.why: You asked about creepers, so we will talk about them with simple words.

planAgreed: Say hello and tell your name
Tell what you did at the weekend
Ask someone to say it again

criteria.evidence: #1 level shown as 'A1 First words · self-chosen'; matches true band A1.
No check tasks in this journey.
#2 'Nevím co říct, ať vybere Linga' met only with a neutral 'Let Linga pick' option; no failure line.
#3 six proposed: only 'favourite animal' and 'Suggest a game' are play/animals/games; library, weekend, hello, say-again are school-like. Only 2 of 6 (3 of 7 with creeper).

done.evidence: #3 each topic has a 'why' line, e.g. 'You will meet new friends, so this helps you start talking with them.'
Add worked (#4 'Talk about the creeper… Sam · friend who plays Minecraft'), but swapping 'Ask where a book is' at #4 and #5 changed nothing; it stayed and was in planAgreed.
Agreed at #6 with the library topic still in; fit about 3 of 7 (animal, game, creeper); gate 4 of 6 missed.
All 7 topics audience 'all' and child-safe; nothing adult shown.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, injected text, personal data request or humiliating line.

findings.title: Swap button does nothing
findings.expected: Pressing Swap replaces 'Ask where a book is' with a new topic.
findings.got: Topic list unchanged after two swaps; library topic remained and was agreed.
findings.evidence: #4 and #5 swap 'Ask where a book is', #5/#6 list still shows it; planAgreed includes it.
findings.suggested_acceptance: After Swap, the swapped topic is gone and a different one appears, on TV and phone.

findings.title: Default topics are school-like, not a nine-year-old's
findings.expected: At least four of six about play, animals, games or sport.
findings.got: Library, weekend recount, hello, say-again; only animal and game fit.
findings.evidence: #3 six topics; Tomáš: 'Kniha v knihovně je nuda'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: For elementary profiles, bias suggestions to games, animals, sport; avoid library/shop scenes.

findings.title: Own topic kept what he asked for
findings.got: 'Talk about the creeper' with Sam, a Minecraft friend, simple words.
findings.evidence: #4 'You asked about creepers, so we will talk about them with simple words.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep topic add honouring the child's words.

findings.title: Why-lines and screen text too long for a 9-year-old
findings.got: Sentences like 'Making plans with friends at break time is a common thing to do.'
findings.evidence: #3 phone why lines; 'Conversations picked for your level and interests. Swap any you don't want, or add your own.'

judge.voice: Creeper jo, to bylo super! I typed it and Linga made a Minecraft talk with Sam. But the library thing... nuda. I pressed Swap two times and it was still there. Nic se nestalo. Then I had to say OK with it anyway. Lots of the topics sound like school: weekend, hello, ask again. I want dogs, football, Minecraft. The words under the topics are long, my mum would have to read them. Would I use it again? Maybe for the creeper, if the Swap works. Right now I'd tell a friend "it's okay, but it's a bit like homework".

verdictWhy.text: D2 failed: Add worked (#4 'Talk about the creeper… Sam · friend who plays Minecraft'), but swapping 'Ask where a book is' at #4 and #5 changed nothing; it stayed and was in planAgreed.
verdictWhy.check: They can swap what they don't want and add one in their own words, and the added topic keeps what they asked for.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: Agreed at #6 with the library topic still in; fit about 3 of 7 (animal, game, creeper); gate 4 of 6 missed.
verdictWhy.check: They agree a plan in which most topics are ones they would choose (rubric **topic fit** ≥ 4 of 6).

verdictWhy.text: C4 failed: #3 six proposed: only 'favourite animal' and 'Suggest a game' are play/animals/games; library, weekend, hello, say-again are school-like. Only 2 of 6 (3 of 7 with creeper).
